subject.title: [Feature]: Pattern-based channel allowlist for Discord (glob/wildcard support)

question: Should Discord dynamic-channel authorization be category-first, or should OpenClaw also support a documented wildcard pattern grammar for channel names?
rationale: Both choices expand an inbound authorization boundary, and repository policy requires intentional ownership, compatibility, and precedence decisions for new config surfaces and fallbacks.

options.title: Adopt category-first rules
options.body: Use stable Discord category IDs for dynamic-channel grouping and defer mutable name-pattern matching unless a remaining workflow cannot be represented safely.

options.title: Approve narrow name patterns
options.body: Add Discord-only pattern entries with a restricted grammar, deterministic ordering, and exact-id/name/parent precedence documented and tested.

options.title: Keep explicit entries only
options.body: Retain the current explicit allowlist and document configuration updates as the supported operator workflow.

recommendation.title: Adopt category-first rules
recommendation.body: Use stable Discord category IDs for dynamic-channel grouping and defer mutable name-pattern matching unless a remaining workflow cannot be represented safely.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature history most strongly connects this person to the shared matcher and Discord allowlist semantics involved in the decision.
